question: ‘Gugga Naumi’ – the festival celebrated in Haryana and some parts of Punjab, Rajasthan, UP and Himachal Pradesh ______ is known as the festival of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**snake worshipping**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gugga Naumi is celebrated as the festival of snake-worshiping.
 
• This festival is observed in honour of Gugga Pir or Gugga Jahar Peer, who is considered a saint in Hindu and Sikh traditions.
 
• It is celebrated in the month of Bhadrapada (August-September) according to the Hindu calendar.
 
• The festival involves singing hymns, offering prayers, and distributing prasad among community members.
 
• Devotees also paint snakes on the walls of their homes as a part of the celebrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Key Figure
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Gugga Pir**
 A revered figure in North India, associated with the worship of snakes and believed to protect his devotees from snake bites.
 
 

 **Festival Time**
 Occurs in the lunar month of **Bhadrapada**, marking the monsoon season when snakes are more active.
 
 

 **Worship Practices**
 Includes creating **snake motifs**, singing devotional songs, and offering milk to snakes.
 
 

 **Geographical Spread**
 Primarily celebrated in **Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh**, and **Himachal Pradesh**.
